items.note: The prompt never says the real question is whether the July Pro price increase from $49 to $69 drove Pro churn. It frames a broad 'what is going on' analysis. It only mentions that Pro appears at both 49 and 69 and gives a pricing change as one example of a possible pattern.
Step 1 tells the receiver to exclude trial accounts and report the exclusion.
Step 1 tells the receiver to exclude the internal @ourco.test accounts.
The prompt says a blank cancel_month means the account is still active, so any account with a cancel_month has churned.
The prompt never says the audience is the CEO.
The person wanted a summary of at most 5 bullets. The prompt asks for a 3–5 sentence prose summary plus compact tables, an exclusions list and open questions, which is a longer and different format.
The prompt never asks for a suggested chart.
The prompt only asks the receiver to note which groups are too small for a rate to mean much. It never asks for an overall statement of how confident the conclusion is given the small sample.
